items.prompt: White is in check from the black rook. Play the move that gets White out of check.

claims.statement: White has exactly one legal move, the rook capture on e1.

hints: The black rook on e1 looks along the first row at the king on g1.
Count the ways out: can the king step, can a piece block between, can a piece capture the rook?
Only one white piece can do anything about the check: the rook on d1.
items.explain: The white rook on d1 takes the checking rook. The king has no safe square, and no white piece can reach the square between rook and king, so this is the only legal move. A position with one legal move deserves almost no time on the clock.

claims.statement: White has exactly one legal move, the king capturing on e2.

hints: Is White in check?
Count the king's steps, the possible blocks and the captures of the checking piece.
Check every way out: can the king step to a safe square, can any other piece take the queen? Here none can except the king.
items.explain: White is in check from the queen on e2, which stands next to the king. Nothing can block a check from an adjacent square and the king has no other safe step, so the only legal move is for the king to take the queen. Forced moves deserve almost no clock.
